setup: Use a slam ball that won't bounce
execution: Reach the ball high overhead, up on your toes
Slam it down hard just in front of your feet
Bend hips and knees as you follow through
Squat to pick it up, then go again
faults: Don't throw it with arms alone
Don't round your back to pick it up
Don't slam it onto your toes

notes: Use a dead-bounce slam ball. A bouncy medicine ball can rebound up into your face.
Slam onto a solid floor with a clear area around you.
Pick the ball up with a squat and a flat back, especially when tired.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move
Chest pain, faintness or unusual breathlessness

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at hip height, figure facing right, with a clear patch of floor just in front of the feet where the ball lands.

keyPositions.label: Reach
keyPositions.describe: Standing tall on the toes, arms straight overhead holding the ball, body in a long line, hips slightly forward.

keyPositions.label: Slam
keyPositions.describe: Arms driven down, ball released and hitting the floor just in front of the feet. Hips back and knees bent, flat back, eyes down at the ball.

keyPositions.label: Pick up
keyPositions.describe: Squatting with a flat back to lift the ball from the floor back to the chest.

ikHints: Ball leaves the hands at the end of the slam and lands on the floor
emphasise: Full reach overhead on the toes
